response.recommendation: Test one stronger protection rule on the frozen Q-RMEA circuit. Preserve both the mention Born intensities and the attention denominator, then learn a small signed movement along the remaining direction that most changes the actual decoder output. This asks whether reallocating a fixed amount of context attention among tokens has predictive value. The most informative control is a direct logit correction that reproduces the circuit rule through first order. If that control captures the gain, stop.

routes.route: Decoder steering at fixed mention attention and fixed context mass
routes.basis: The full run beat the native reference by 0.01334 macro-F1, but lost to scrambled context by 0.01149 and to unprotected context by 0.00793. CE gave the same ordering. That removes the empirical rationale for pursuing context-power suppression as the objective. The actual 12-angle circuit did establish finite, decoder-visible motion on 31 of 32 selected TRAIN cases under raw mention protection. Its logit changes had both signs. The added denominator constraint targets a question those results leave open. Can the circuit move the logit by changing which context tokens receive attention while leaving every mention weight fixed?
routes.plugin: For one example and relation, let p_i(θ)=|ψ_iᴴφ(θ)|² over valid tokens, Z=Σ_i(p_i+EPS), and L=b+Σ_i(p_i+EPS)u_i/Z. With mention set M and context set C, constrain F(θ)=( (p_j)_{j∈M}, Σ_{i∈C}p_i ) to its native value. Exact feasibility fixes Z, every normalized mention weight, and total normalized context mass. The finite logit change then satisfies ΔL=Σ_{i∈C}(u_i−c)Δp_i/Z for any constant c. This is a checkable readout identity on each example. The plugin uses one learned signed scalar per relation, shared across examples. Its sign and magnitude are fitted on training labels. At inference its direction depends only on native states, roles and decoder utilities.

response.theory: There is a sharp local cost for adding denominator protection. Work at the native angles on a regular branch. Let D=∂φ/∂θ, H=(I−φφᴴ)D, and G=Re(HᴴH). Assume G is positive definite and use ||δθ||_G as the first-order physical state displacement, which discounts global phase. In whitened coordinates x=G^(1/2)δθ, let P be the orthogonal projector onto ker(J_M G^(−1/2)), where J_M contains the mention-intensity rows. Define a=P G^(−1/2)∇L and h=P G^(−1/2)∇Σ_C p_i. Raw mention protection alone permits a maximum first-order logit increase of s||a|| at displacement budget s. Adding fixed context mass gives exactly sκ, where v=a−h(hᵀa)/||h||² and κ=||v|| for h≠0. For h=0 take v=a. Proof follows by maximizing aᵀx on the radius-s ball in the mention kernel intersected with h⊥. For κ>0 the maximizing angle direction is d=G^(−1/2)v/κ. Thus the squared steering capacity lost is exactly (hᵀa)²/||h||² when h≠0. When a≠0, κ²/||a||² measures the fraction retained. This gives an example- and relation-specific prediction from the frozen module before fitting. On a regular exact fiber the optimal local slope is attainable, so the finite expansion along that direction is ΔL=sκ+O(s²). The projection argument uses standard geometry. Its research value here is the quantitative distinction between moving total context mass and redistributing that mass through the reachable circuit and its decoder.
counterexamples: If every context token has the same utility for a relation, exact redistribution gives ΔL=0 at every feasible step, even when context probabilities move substantially. With only one context token there is no redistribution at all.

If a is parallel to a nonzero h, the extra constraint consumes all first-order steering capacity. If they are orthogonal, its first-order cost is zero. Both outcomes are compatible with the previous 31 positive cases.

With 12 physical angle directions, m independent mention rows and one further independent mass row leave 11−m tangent dimensions. At m=11 that branch has no steering direction. Singular certainty constraints or phase-identifying measurements can also eliminate motion. The previous physical rank of 12 does not establish regularity of the augmented constraints.
response.implementation:
Freeze token preparation, base effects, utilities and decoder. Cache φ and the eight-complex-by-12 derivative D once per base relation. Obtain its columns by analytic gate differentiation or 12 batched forward-mode directions. For every valid token form z_i=ψ_iᴴφ and J_i=2 Re[conj(z_i) ψ_iᴴD] by contraction. The exact native gradient is ∇L=Σ_i(u_i−(L−b))J_i/Z. These operations give all projections without a reverse Jacobian per example. Use small rank-revealing solves grouped by mention count. For this first test, admit only well-conditioned G and full-row-rank augmented constraints with a resolved nonzero kernel and κ. Return the native row on every other branch and retain it in the denominators. This conservative rule can exclude genuinely movable rank-deficient cases.

Use t_r=s_max tanh(β_r), initialized at zero, and propose θ₁=θ₀+t_r d. Apply exactly two fixed-base chord corrections θ←θ−B(F(θ)−F(θ₀)), with B the minimum-G-norm right inverse of the augmented native Jacobian. Evaluate the final state and logits through the original two-layer, three-qubit circuit, including EPS and the valid-token mask. Candidate states change per example, so only the base states and derivatives are shared. Batch or chunk the candidate forwards. Admit a finite step only within the source angle range, the declared physical displacement budget up to numerical tolerance, and the residual tolerances for both raw constraints and normalized mention weights. Otherwise use the native row. Two corrections give measured finite preservation. Under bounded second derivatives and a bounded right inverse, the initial O(t²) residual contracts by O(|t|) per fixed-base correction locally. That gives O(t⁴) after two corrections, with no global guarantee.

In this frozen-base experiment the cached derivatives are constants with respect to β. Differentiate through both candidate corrections and the final circuit readout. No Hessian or detached surrogate is needed for the actual fitted parameters. Joint fitting of base effects or token preparation would require mixed second derivatives through J, G, ∇L and the solves on stable-rank branches. The hard fallback also makes the implemented map piecewise smooth. The steering theorem applies on admitted regular branches; the end-to-end evaluation must include fallback behavior.
response.discriminating_test:
Run one bounded frozen-head pilot if separately authorized. First use the existing TRAIN32 solely for an engineering check of the stronger constraint. Proposed fixed settings are float64, s_max=10⁻³ in the physical metric, two corrections, a 10⁻¹² maximum absolute residual for each raw constraint and normalized mention weight, and a 10⁻⁶ minimum relative singular value for each required full-rank solve. Check gradients of a scalar loss against central differences in β on admitted nonzero steps away from fallback boundaries. Stop before fitting if no row passes at a nonzero step, the gradient check fails, or a batch of eight examples across all 40 relations cannot complete forward and backward on one existing 3060 using relation chunking. No larger solver or replacement cohort is part of this pilot.

For the utility comparison, predeclare a bounded slice, split, one training pass, step budget and paired CE endpoint before examining labels or new outputs. Fit the 40 scalars separately in each arm with identical examples, initialization, optimizer and update count. Compare the finite circuit rule with (1) native logits, (2) L+t_rκ, the direct logit control with the same first-order response and the same finite-step admission rule at its own proposed t_r, and (3) the same finite circuit update with the context-mass constraint removed. The third arm measures the cost or benefit of fixing normalized mention attention. Before fitting, record κ, retained capacity and the discrepancy ΔL−tκ at a fixed nonzero step. After fitting, verify the finite redistribution identity to the tolerance implied by the measured residuals. Report paired CE contrasts, macro-F1, and admission and fallback rates across the entire declared slice. Give the eligible-domain result alongside its population coverage. The original 663/58,465 figure describes the earlier input filter only.

Advance this particular mechanism only if the finite rule improves held-out CE against native and both fitted controls, with paired uncertainty supporting the direction. A tie with the direct logit control answers the most important question even if both beat native. A loss to the raw-only arm removes the utility rationale for the stronger protection rule. Treat any reused or previously inspected split as development evidence. Independent support would require freezing the same circuit rule and controls before evaluation on untouched examples, with independent training replication before a general performance claim.
response.novelty_status: The candidate contribution is the fixed-attention redistribution rule together with a prediction of its reachable decoder gain and a control that can explain away its apparent utility. Phase-retrieval fibers, metric projection, constrained beamforming and chord correction are established tools. The supplied reading leaves the quadratically constrained beamforming neighbor unresolved at the formula level. A substantive nearest-neighbor difference still needs to be established against its actual objective, constraints and update, and against direct decoder correction empirically.
response.claim_ceiling: L5 remains NOT_ACCEPTED. The strongest current implementation evidence is finite raw-intensity preservation with a visible class-0 logit change in 31 evaluated cases on an exposed TRAIN cohort. One selected m=13 case was inapplicable. The stronger normalized-attention rule, its trainability, its utility and its independent support are all untested. No tools were run or code changed.
